topics.description: Visual polish, material, theme, typography, color, spacing, icons and content presentation. Prefer visual-qa for accepted designs; create-design for a requested proposal; design-system for a reusable rule.
Component variants and loading, empty, error, disabled, selected, pending and completed states; distinguish feature behavior from reusable component rules.

Forms, parameter configuration and schema-driven inspectors. Bind parameter identity, type, units, constraints, options, value source, per-parameter control, validation, save/reset and observed persistence; generic record editing is not sufficient for differing semantics.
Search, filters, sorting, pickers, selections and command interfaces; distinguish query/result/selection, retained context, keyboard behavior, async and no-result states.

Navigation, sidebar, workspace layout, right inspector, split view, drawer and modal. Compare task co-presence, usable content width, interruption, unsaved state, dismiss/back and focus rather than choosing from a control name.
Object/action/task hierarchy, permissions, route structure or workflow steps. Separate unresolved product behavior from the Design layout; use existing Discovery only for decisions that require it.

Responsive and narrow viewport behavior, touch/pointer, keyboard, focus, assistive paths and reduced motion. Require actual affected modes and viewport/state evidence, not source or build proof alone.
Charts, dashboards, dense tables, comparisons and records. Bind data meaning, units, scale, partial/stale/error states and an accessible equivalent to the user's decision.

Graph, canvas, spatial editor or timeline. Bind selection, zoom/pan, edits, undo/recovery, retained workspace, large/empty data and a keyboard/nonspatial alternative. A UI view does not require a new graph store.

Web, mobile, desktop or operational app patterns. Bind the real actor, platform, domain objects, task frequency, density, side effects and constraints; reuse accepted target systems instead of a universal CRUD or marketing composition.
